title: Adhikari says he will name ward coordinators from 1 December if Howrah and Kolkata polls stay stalled
dek: The chief minister said only people who 'stand by the government' would be picked. Trinamool, the CPI(M) and the Congress objected; the BJP says its own leaders will fill the posts.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has said his government will appoint coordinators for the wards of the Howrah and Kolkata municipal corporations from 1 December if elections to the two civic bodies cannot be held by then. He said those chosen would be people who back the government.

"We will appoint only those as coordinators who stand by the government and do not oppose it," Mr Adhikari said on Thursday at a Chhath Puja programme at Kazipara in Howrah, according to reports. He said municipal corporations could not be run indefinitely by officials, who cannot fully replace elected representatives.

## A new deadline

The announcement moves the date the chief minister had set earlier. On 6 November, after the Calcutta High Court stopped the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) election from being called, he said he would wait until 13 November before appointing coordinators for all 209 of Kolkata's newly drawn wards. On Thursday he named 1 December instead.

Reports differ on the scope. One report said Thursday's remarks covered the Howrah Municipal Corporation alone; others said they covered every ward in both Howrah and Kolkata. He described the coordinators as an interim arrangement until elections are held.

Mr Adhikari repeated that the state would go to the Supreme Court against the High Court's order and said legal redress would come first, according to reports. One report said he referred to a special leave petition and to the court's vacation bench. None of the reports said a petition had been filed.

"Those who are likely to lose their security deposits in the elections are the ones obstructing the process," he said, according to reports, accusing opposition parties of using the courts to delay the vote.

## Why the polls are stuck

Kolkata has had no elected council since June, when the corporation was dissolved and an administrator appointed. The state then raised the number of wards from 144 to 209. On 6 November a Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee barred the State Election Commission from notifying the KMC election on the new ward map until a single judge decides a challenge to it, filed by former CPI(M) councillor Dipu Das. According to reports, the bench also said an administrator running a dissolved corporation may exercise its executive functions but not its legislative powers.

Howrah has gone longer without councillors. It last voted in 2013, and its elected board's term ended in 2018, since when it has been run by government-appointed officials, according to reports. The state had earlier indicated that Howrah and Bally could vote by December once wards were redrawn there. Mr Adhikari said Howrah residents had been without proper civic representation for about 12 years.

## Reactions

BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya backed the plan. "Our own leaders will become coordinators," he said, according to reports, adding that the party would not pick people from the CPI(M) or those he described as corrupt Trinamool figures.

Trinamool Congress leader Baishwanar Chattopadhyay said the government was "simply looking for 'yes-men'", according to reports, and his colleague Krishanu Moitra said the BJP wanted "a BJP administrator in each ward". CPI(M) leader Chayan Bhattacharya said his party strongly objected, and Sujan Chakraborty of the CPI(M) accused the BJP of running municipalities through handpicked people. Congress leader Ashutosh Chattopadhyay called the ward redrawing "unscientific", according to reports.

## What happens next

The state's appeal to the Supreme Court, if filed, and the single-judge hearing on the ward map will decide whether the Kolkata vote can be called. Mr Adhikari said he would inspect Chhath ghats on the Hooghly by boat on the evening of 15 November.
